input.question: Why aren't high rise office fires more common/unsurvivable?
input.ground_truth: They used to, then builders got wise to it. Now we build high rises out of concrete and glass, which don't catch on fire. We restrict how much flammable material is used on the floors of high rises and don't allow anything flammable at all in the stairwells (that's why the stairs are pretty much always barren concrete with metal railings), which makes it more difficult for the fires to spread between floors.

response.prediction: High-rise office fires are not as common or as deadly as people might think because modern buildings are designed with safety in mind. They have advanced fire detection and alarm systems that alert everyone quickly if a fire starts. Buildings also have automatic sprinkler systems that can put out small fires before they grow. Fire doors, fire-resistant materials, and clearly marked, well-maintained escape routes help people get out safely. Additionally, fire departments are trained to respond to high-rise fires with special equipment and procedures. Because of these safety measures, most high-rise office fires are contained or controlled before they become large or deadly.
